metadata.title: Reverse Transcription: First-Strand cDNA Synthesis (SuperScript First-Strand Synthesis System for RT-PCR)
metadata.purpose: Synthesize first-strand cDNA from total or poly(A)+ RNA using SuperScript II Reverse Transcriptase primed with oligo(dT) (or a gene-specific primer), producing single-stranded cDNA suitable for downstream PCR (RT-PCR).
metadata.scope: First-strand cDNA synthesis with the SuperScript First-Strand Synthesis System for RT-PCR (Cat. no. 11904-018), oligo(dT)12-18 priming path, for 1 ng-5 ug total RNA or 50-500 ng poly(A)+ RNA. Random-hexamer priming is captured as a branch. Downstream target PCR itself is out of scope (only the kit's control PCR is described).
metadata.estimatedTime: ~1.5 h (RNA/primer denaturation, 42 C/50 min synthesis, termination, RNase H step)
beforeYouBegin: Use high-quality, intact, RNase-free RNA; work with RNase-free technique and reagents.
If genomic DNA carryover must be eliminated, pre-treat the RNA with DNase I (Amplification Grade) before starting.
Choose the priming strategy: oligo(dT) is recommended for new mRNA targets; random hexamers for difficult/long or non-polyadenylated templates; gene-specific primer for maximum specificity.

materials.name: Oligo(dT)12-18 primer
materials.specification: 0.5 ug/uL stock; anneals to 3' poly(A) tails of mRNA

materials.name: Random hexamers
materials.specification: 50 ng/uL stock; nonspecific priming (alternative to oligo(dT))

materials.name: 10X RT buffer
materials.rawText: 10X RT buffer*  ... *200 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.4), 500 mM KCl

materials.name: SuperScript II Reverse Transcriptase
materials.specification: 50 U/uL; RNase H-reduced MMLV RT; usable up to 50 C

materials.name: E. coli RNase H
materials.specification: 2 U/uL; degrades RNA in the RNA:cDNA hybrid after synthesis
materials.rawText: E. coli RNase H (2 U/ul) 50 ul

materials.name: Control RNA
materials.specification: 50 ng/uL; positive-control template (use 1 uL); yields a 500-bp product with Control Primers A+B

materials.name: Control Primer A (antisense)
materials.specification: 10 uM; sequence 5'-GAC ATG GAA GCC ATC ACA GAC-3'
materials.rawText: Control Primer A: 5'-GAC ATG GAA GCC ATC ACA GAC-3'

materials.name: Control Primer B (sense)
materials.specification: 10 uM; sequence 5'-AGA CCG TTC AGC TGG ATA TTA C-3'
materials.rawText: Control Primer B: 5'-AGA CCG TTC AGC TGG ATA TTA C-3'

equipment.name: Thermal cycler or water baths/heat blocks

samples.name: Total RNA
samples.description: 1 ng-5 ug total RNA (or 50-500 ng poly(A)+ RNA) per reaction; e.g. RNA from a TRIzol extraction.

samples.name: RNA/primer mix (annealed)
samples.description: RNA + oligo(dT) + dNTPs denatured at 65 C then snap-cooled on ice.

samples.name: First-strand cDNA
samples.description: Single-stranded first-strand cDNA; store at -20 C or use directly in PCR (use ~10% / 2 uL per PCR).

containers.name: Sterile 0.2 or 0.5 mL microcentrifuge / thin-walled PCR tube

tables.title: RNA/primer mix (per reaction, oligo(dT) or GSP path)
rows: Oligo(dT)12-18 (0.5 ug/uL) or 2 uM gene-specific primer

tables.title: 2X reaction mix (add components in the order listed)
tables.note: 9 uL of this 2X mix is added to each 10 uL RNA/primer mix.

steps.action: In a sterile PCR tube, combine the RNA/primer mix per the table: n uL RNA (1 ng-5 ug), 1 uL 10 mM dNTP mix, 1 uL oligo(dT)12-18 (0.5 ug/uL), and DEPC-treated water to 10 uL.

branches.condition: If priming with random hexamers instead of oligo(dT)
branches.action: Use 1-5 uL random hexamers (50 ng/uL) in place of oligo(dT), and after adding RT (step 6) add a 25 C / 10 min incubation before the 42 C / 50 min synthesis.

steps.action: Incubate the RNA/primer mix at 65 C for 5 min to denature secondary structure, then place on ice for at least 1 min.

parameters.rawText: on ice for at least 1 minute

steps.action: In a separate tube, prepare the 2X reaction mix per the table, adding components in the order listed: 2 uL 10X RT buffer, 4 uL 25 mM MgCl2, 2 uL 0.1 M DTT, 1 uL RNaseOUT (per reaction).
steps.criticalNotes: Add components in the indicated order. Scale by the number of reactions (see 10-reaction column).

steps.action: Add 9 uL of the 2X reaction mix to each RNA/primer mix, mix gently, and collect by brief centrifugation.

parameters.rawText: Add 9 ul of the 2X reaction mix to each RNA/primer mixture

steps.action: Incubate at 42 C for 2 min to equilibrate.
Add 1 uL SuperScript II RT to each tube (for the minus-RT control, add 1 uL DEPC-treated water instead).

parameters.rawText: Add 1 ul of SuperScript II RT to each tube

steps.criticalNotes: Include a minus-RT control (water instead of RT) to detect genomic-DNA-derived signal in downstream PCR.

steps.action: Incubate at 42 C for 50 min to synthesize first-strand cDNA.
steps.expectedResult: First-strand cDNA synthesized along the RNA template.

steps.action: Terminate the reaction at 70 C for 15 min, then chill on ice.
Collect by brief centrifugation, add 1 uL E. coli RNase H to each tube, and incubate at 37 C for 20 min to remove RNA from the RNA:cDNA hybrid.

parameters.rawText: Add 1 ul of RNase H to each tube

steps.criticalNotes: The reaction can be stored at -20 C or used for PCR immediately (use ~10% / 2 uL per 50 uL PCR).
steps.expectedResult: Single-stranded first-strand cDNA ready for PCR.

controls.name: Minus-RT control
controls.description: Parallel reaction with DEPC-treated water in place of SuperScript II RT; downstream PCR signal indicates genomic-DNA contamination rather than cDNA.

controls.name: Plus-RT positive control (Control RNA)
controls.description: 1 uL Control RNA (50 ng/uL) reverse-transcribed then amplified with Control Primers A+B gives a 500-bp product, confirming the first-strand reaction worked.

expectedOutputs: First-strand cDNA suitable for PCR (use ~10% / 2 uL of the reaction per PCR).
For the kit control: a 500-bp band from Control RNA in the plus-RT reaction, with the minus-RT band <=50% of that intensity.

troubleshooting.cause: Procedural error or RNase contamination in first-strand synthesis; too little cDNA used in PCR
troubleshooting.solution: Verify with Control RNA; use RNaseOUT and aseptic technique; use up to 10 uL of the first-strand reaction in PCR

troubleshooting.cause: Genomic DNA contamination of the RNA
troubleshooting.solution: Pre-treat RNA with DNase I (Amplification Grade); design primers spanning an intron/exon-exon boundary

troubleshooting.problem: Short or truncated cDNA / strong transcriptional pauses
troubleshooting.cause: Stable RNA secondary structure or high GC content
troubleshooting.solution: Raise synthesis temperature toward 50 C (SuperScript II) or use SuperScript III (42-55 C); consider random hexamers

safety: DTT is an irritant; wear gloves and eye protection.
Maintain RNase-free technique; handle all reagents per institutional chemical-safety rules.
limitations: SuperScript II RT is usable only up to 50 C, so very GC-rich or highly structured templates may transcribe poorly (SuperScript III / Thermo-X are recommended for higher temperatures). Genomic DNA is not removed unless the RNA is DNase-treated. Exact RNA input, primer choice, and downstream PCR conditions are target-dependent.
